Definition: from G2596; and ἧμαι (to sit; akin to the base of G1476); to sit down; figuratively, to remain, reside:--dwell, sit (by, down).
BiblicalUsage: To sit down is what the Son of man will do at the right hand of power, and the high priest heard it from His own mouth, and Paul says to seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God. The word holds the trial and the throne together: the One they condemned is the One who sits, and the sitting is the verdict on the trial.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the seated Christ is the proof that the trial was wrong and the cross was right. I hold that my life is hid with Him where He sits, and I will set my mind on the things above, not on the things of the earth.
